method.summary: Delivery episodes were grouped by shared changed paths and resolvable commit or pull-request evidence, then compared with exactly bound graph components. A proposal was retained only when structural and delivery evidence overlapped.

hypotheses.label: Client record search and result browsing
hypotheses.user_product_value: A user can search client records by a name prefix, receive normalized matching behavior, and browse a paginated result set.
hypotheses.structural_delivery_convergence: The graph exposes a find-form path into paginated owner lookup and a repository prefix-search operation; delivery episodes added owner-list pagination and later corrected whitespace handling on the same controller path.

confidence.rationale: Two temporally distinct delivery episodes overlap the bound controller and repository components, including one narrowly scoped pull request.

limitations: The graph has no direct controller-to-repository call edge, so the repository association is supported by co-change and naming rather than a graph path.
The graph does not index the HTML templates, so the visible pagination experience is inferred from delivery paths and subjects.
This proposal does not establish the Product Team's preferred terminology or boundary.

hypotheses.label: Companion record identity and update safeguards
hypotheses.user_product_value: A user can create or update a companion record while the system protects per-client name uniqueness, persisted associations, and basic name validity.
hypotheses.structural_delivery_convergence: Bound create and update handlers call duplicate-name and update paths, while owner association and validator nodes are present; four linked delivery episodes exercise duplicate-name behavior, persisted association, name validation, and update regression coverage.

confidence.rationale: Multiple narrowly scoped commits and pull requests align with the exact bound controller, owner, and validator components, including repeated regression evidence.

limitations: Database uniqueness scripts and test behavior are delivery evidence but are not represented as graph nodes in the Java-only graph.
The graph does not provide cross-file edges between the controller, owner entity, and validator; convergence depends on shared delivery episodes.
The proposal intentionally does not decide whether creation, update, and validation are one Product Capability or several.

hypotheses.label: Visit date intake safeguards
hypotheses.user_product_value: A user can record a visit with date constraints that reject unsupported future dates before the visit is accepted.
hypotheses.structural_delivery_convergence: The bound graph contains visit date accessors and controller nodes for minimum-date calculation and new-visit processing; one focused pull request changed both Java components together to validate future dates.

confidence.rationale: A focused commit and pull request overlap both structural components and state the same date constraint visible in the bound node names.

limitations: Only one delivery episode is cited, so independent repetition is absent.
No cross-file graph edge connects the visit entity and controller in this extraction.
The exact business exception policy and user wording are not established by the frozen evidence.

hypotheses.label: Practitioner directory and specialty presentation
hypotheses.user_product_value: A user can browse a paginated practitioner directory and view practitioner specialties in a predictable order and machine-readable representation.
hypotheses.structural_delivery_convergence: The graph connects list display to pagination and exposes resource-list, repository-list, collection, and specialty-access nodes; delivery history co-changed the directory components for pagination and later refined specialty ordering and controller representation handling.

confidence.rationale: The structural cluster is broad and delivery evidence spans pagination plus two maintenance-oriented episodes rather than a single explicit end-to-end feature.

limitations: The pagination commit is broad and changes owner, visit, cache, and practitioner paths together, weakening boundary precision.
Two cited pull requests are maintenance or refactoring changes and do not independently prove an end-user capability.
The HTML and serialized representations are not nodes in the Java-only graph.

hypotheses.label: Locale-selectable presentation
hypotheses.user_product_value: A user can select a locale and receive translated interface text across multiple presentation surfaces.
hypotheses.structural_delivery_convergence: The graph exposes locale resolution and locale-change interception registered in web configuration; one linked delivery episode changed that same configuration alongside multiple translation bundles and presentation templates.

confidence.rationale: The structural locale controls and delivery paths align directly, but only one linked episode is cited and resources are outside the Java graph.

limitations: Translation completeness and runtime rendering are not proven by the Java-only graph.
Only one delivery episode overlaps the web configuration and localized resources in this proposal.
Language coverage and terminology remain Product Team review questions.

unresolved_boundaries.reason: Client, companion, and visit components share paths and aggregate-style delivery history, but their focused delivery episodes and graph communities remain distinct; no merge is forced.
Directory presentation can be localized, but structural locale controls and directory delivery episodes do not justify collapsing the two proposals.

global_limitations: The graph contains deterministic Java AST evidence only and has no embedded Git revision metadata; exact binding is supplied by the frozen live-evidence record and digest.
Pull-request coverage is limited to the frozen dataset's acquisition boundary.
No Product Semantics, evaluator truth, forward output, post-cutoff knowledge, or historical reverse output was used.
These are blinded proposals for human review, not accepted or published Product truth.
